rationale: Across both syndromic juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis and non-syndromic CLN3-associated retinal dystrophy (RP101 / isolated CLN3 disease), electroretinography does not display an invariable, uniform rod-cone photoreceptor pattern. Instead, literature across multiple independent cohorts demonstrates that CLN3 disease manifests heterogeneous and stage-dependent ERG findings: classic rod-cone dystrophy patterns (as seen in middle-aged adult non-syndromic cohorts), prominent electronegative waveforms indicating selective or disproportionate b-wave inner-retinal transmission deficits, and completely undetectable or extinguished responses in advanced degeneration.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 15 patients with non-syndromic isolated retinal degeneration caused by biallelic CLN3 variants, retinal disease exhibited two distinct functional patterns (mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset in 6 patients, and severe early macular atrophic degeneration in 9 patients), with documented electronegative ERG configuration in individual patients.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Two distinct patterns of retinal disease could be identified: a mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset (n = 6; legal blindness threshold reached by 70s) and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n = 9; legal blindness threshold reached by 40s)... Patient CIC03517 had a clearly electronegative ERG (b wave less than a wave)

evidence.text: In eight children with CLN3 disease, electroretinography did not show an isolated rod-cone photoreceptor deficit; an electronegative ERG was present in 4 patients (50%), and the remaining 4 patients (50%) had an undetectable ERG due to advanced outer retinal degeneration.

source.title: Juvenile Batten disease (CLN3): detailed ocular phenotype, novel observations, delayed diagnosis, masquerades, and prospects for therapy
source.quote: An electronegative ERG was present in 4 patients (50%), but with additional a-wave reduction, there was an undetectable ERG in the remaining 4 patients.

evidence.text: In children presenting with CLN3 disease compared to early-onset Stargardt disease (STGD1), dark-adapted full-field ERG responses were either undetectable/absent or electronegative in CLN3 disease, distinguishing it reliably from STGD1.

source.title: Recognizing differentiating clinical signs of CLN3 disease (Batten disease) at presentation
source.quote: In CLN3 disease, dark-adapted (DA) full-field electroretinogram (ERG) responses were either absent or electronegative. In early-onset STGD1, DA ERG responses were generally unaffected. None of the STGD1 patients had an electronegative ERG.

evidence.text: A 50-year-old adult presenting with non-syndromic CLN3 retinal dystrophy (harboring the classic 1.02 kb deletion in trans with c.175G>A) exhibited rod and secondary cone degeneration where full-field ERG responses progressively deteriorated into an electronegative configuration over clinical follow-up.

source.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of non-syndromic retinal dystrophy due to c.175G>A mutation in ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 3 (CLN3)
source.quote: ERG responses became electronegative and patient's serum contained anti-retinal antibodies... non-syndromic CLN3 disease leads to rod and delayed primary cone degeneration resulting in constricting peripheral field and enlarging central scotoma

evidence.text: Visual electrophysiology in pediatric CLN3 presentations demonstrated that all 5 examined patients exhibited electronegative full-field ERGs along with foveal ellipsoid zone disruptions and bull's eye maculopathy.

source.title: Early recognition of CLN3 disease facilitated by visual electrophysiology and multimodal imaging
source.quote: Electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients. Bull's eye maculopathies found in all patients.

evidence.text: Full-field ERG analysis in JNCL showed early severe b-wave reduction relative to a-waves resulting in electronegative waveforms prior to complete response ablation.

source.title: The dystrophic retina in multisystem disorders: the electroretinogram in neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
source.quote: Patients with JNCL invariably showed severe to profound ERG abnormalities when first tested, with essentially no rod-mediated activity and marked loss of a-wave amplitudes with even greater loss of b-wave amplitudes, creating electronegative configuration waveforms... and eventually is totally ablated.

new_directions.question_text: What specific non-null missense or splicing variants in CLN3 preserve sufficient protein function to limit disease to isolated RP/retinal degeneration while delaying or preventing neurodegenerative CNS involvement?
new_directions.rationale: Smirnov et al. (2021) and Chen et al. (2019) observed that patients with isolated CLN3 retinitis pigmentosa carry specific point or hypomorphic mutations rather than the common homozygous 1.02 kb deletion, explaining differences between isolated RP101 and classic Batten disease.

new_directions.question_text: What cellular mechanism within the inner nuclear layer underlies the transient electronegative ERG stage before total photoreceptor ablation in CLN3 retinopathies?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the electronegative ERG stems from primary bipolar cell lysosomal storage pathology or secondary synaptic transmission block will elucidate CLN3 function in retinal circuitry.
